alternate_path_validation.evidence: A complete ARM branch scan of decoded overlay 7 found one direct BL to the battle constructor. The tutorial built-in skip was exercised after the normal constructor and Gate calculation, and the owner fields remained intact through skip completion.
alternate_path_validation.scripted_behavior: The built-in tutorial skip does not bypass owner derivation. No alternate overlay-7 constructor or later overwrite of battle object +0x04/+0x06 was found.

battle_object_fields.initialization: Zeroed at 0x0223CFFC, then assigned from the owner participant's Gate slot at 0x0223D1CC.
battle_object_fields.lifetime: Valid from constructor assignment through battle result and final scene state; invalid after battle-object destruction.
battle_object_fields.reset: The deleting destructor releases the object without clearing this field. A new constructor zeroes it before deriving the next active Gate.

destruction.evidence: The class vtable points to the two cleanup functions. They destroy fourteen child entries, release the objects at +0x6C and +0x70, and the deleting form releases the battle object itself. Neither function rewrites +0x04 or +0x06.
destruction.validity_rule: Memory contents may remain visible after scene completion, but they are stale once the object is destroyed and must not be used as live context.

instruction_evidence.purpose: zero active Gate ID and owner fields during construction
derive owner and Gate ID from arena placement and participant data
allocate the 116-byte battle object and invoke its sole overlay-7 constructor call
final state marks the owning scene complete without rewriting Gate ID or owner

supported_conclusions: Battle object +0x06 is stable for the full live battle-object lifetime and remains valid through result processing and final scene state.
Battle object +0x04 remains paired with the same owner and Gate throughout that lifetime.
The arena-placement owner byte remains stable while separate transient placement-state bytes are cleared during final processing.
The built-in tutorial skip occurs downstream of normal owner derivation and does not bypass or replace the owner fields.
Overlay 7 has one battle-object construction call, and no later class-code write changes +0x04 or +0x06.
Reset is constructor-based: the next battle object is zero-initialized before owner derivation. Destruction ends validity rather than zeroing stale memory.
